details.description: ft:gpt-4.1 is OpenAI's fine-tuning offering built on gpt-4.1-2025-04-14, the GPT-4.1 snapshot released April 14, 2025 with a June 1, 2024 knowledge cutoff. Rather than a chat endpoint to call directly, it is the base model developers use OpenAI's supervised or preference (DPO) fine-tuning to train a custom ft:-prefixed model on their own data. Unlike GPT-3.5 Turbo and GPT-4's original 0613 snapshots, plain gpt-4.1 remains one of the models OpenAI's current fine-tuning documentation lists as an active supervised- and preference-fine-tuning base, alongside gpt-4.1-mini and gpt-4.1-nano, though OpenAI has begun winding down the fine-tuning platform overall and no longer accepts new fine-tuning customers.
advantages: One of the models OpenAI's current fine-tuning documentation still lists as an active supervised fine-tuning and direct preference optimization (DPO) base, alongside gpt-4.1-mini and gpt-4.1-nano.
Inherits gpt-4.1's context window up to 1,047,576 tokens and June 1, 2024 knowledge cutoff, per OpenAI's model documentation.

OpenAI's fine-tuning guide recommends supervised fine-tuning on this base for classification, nuanced translation, generating content in a specific format, and correcting instruction-following failures.
The underlying gpt-4.1 model scores 54.6% on SWE-bench Verified and 90.2% on MMLU, per OpenAI's own launch announcement.
disadvantages: OpenAI is winding down its fine-tuning platform: it is no longer accessible to new users, though existing users can keep creating training jobs 'for the coming months,' per OpenAI's fine-tuning guide.
OpenAI's guide notes fine-tuning gains are not guaranteed below roughly 50 well-crafted demonstration examples.
A third-party comparison reports the underlying gpt-4.1 model trails competitors on some reasoning (GPQA) and coding (SWE-bench) benchmarks despite its strong MMLU score.
use_cases: Fine-tuning to generate content in a specific format

notes: Catalog's empty deprecation_date matches what was found: OpenAI's deprecations page lists gpt-4.1-nano (and ft-gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14) for an October 23, 2026 shutdown, but plain gpt-4.1 / ft-gpt-4.1 do not appear in any deprecation table, and gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 is still listed as a live supervised- and DPO-fine-tuning base. Evaluations describe the underlying gpt-4.1 chat model's benchmark results, which also apply to this fine-tuning base since it is the same weights prior to any customer fine-tuning; both scores (54.6% SWE-bench Verified, 90.2% MMLU) are confirmed on OpenAI's own 'Introducing GPT-4.1 in the API' launch post, so evaluations now cite that maker page directly instead of the third-party blogs that had reported the same figures. Removed the unsupported 'evaluate against the base model' clause from a disadvantage: neither the supervised fine-tuning guide nor the model-optimization guide states it.
